findings.evidence: template/scripts/agent_board.py cmd_hand_off: `if not path.exists(): return 0` and `if item is None: ... return 0`. The caller passes `--quiet`, so the missing-item message is also suppressed. `cmd_reactivate`, by contrast, fails explicitly.
findings.summary: `agent_board.py hand-off` returns 0 when the board file or item is missing. `finish_task.hand_off_board` then reports a successful handoff, but no handed-off record exists, so the next re-handoff still needs a manual `start`. This is the failure the change is meant to remove, and it is silent, which the no-fallback rule discourages.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/agent_board.py rehandoff_refusal: `queue._latest(worktree, number, queue._comments(worktree, queue._repo(worktree), number))` and `queue._is_ancestor(...)`. tests/test_rehandoff_board.py mocks all of them, so no test exercises the real signatures.
findings.summary: The board module's scope gate now depends on private helpers of `publication_queue`: `_latest`, `_comments`, `_repo`, `_is_ancestor`. It makes a network `gh` call on every preflight of a handed-off claim. A rename in the queue module would break the preflight, and nothing but mocked tests guards that.

findings.evidence: agent_board.py claim_eligibility: the handed-off branch precedes the `degraded` return, and `TERMINAL_BOARD_PROBLEMS = frozenset({"merged-branch", "merged-pr"})`. The refusal text in `_required_scope_inputs` says "remove the record with ... agent_board.py finish --id".
findings.summary: A handed-off record whose PR is closed without merging is classified `handed-off`, not `degraded`. Only merged-branch and merged-pr problems make it terminal, so nothing reclaims such a record automatically. The scope gate then refuses with a manual `agent_board.py finish` instruction, which is a manual step for the abandoned-PR case.
